title: Frankie Duson and hotel New Year's jobs
summary: Remarks on Frankie Duson's habits, and the band's yearly Christmas and New Year's Eve jobs at hotels paying $25.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Need music to make a living.

So did Frankie Dooson need music to make a living? That's all I know was a dude. Never knew him to work. He had so many women to say, but he wasn't much of his act like that. He had no clothes, you know. Then he'd come and tell stories. When you think you're out, he'd go tell your people, you let him the trombone, he'd point it to you. But he said, you ain't home, you go there and get it and say, he told him to come there and get it. But we didn't tell him, you know. We quit him after that, you know. He was quite bigotty too. Yeah, yeah. I used to have plenty of jobs. We'd get a job sometimes for them big, just like cotton exchange, you know. That's how I did. We'd get $25. That's all. We'd be late sometimes. We'd play the star banger. That's all they wanted to play. Now, we'd play that. Sometimes we'd just take your time to put the trombone out and go, ahhh. He got his 25 dollars. I had that job. I had that job for five years. Every Christmas, Eve, and every New Year's Eve. They used to hire us, you know, like that. They had different places. They had Catmister, St. Charles Hotel, the Roosevelt Hotel, the Milano Hotel. There's about two other hotels. It used to be different places sometimes. They were getting a job.
